blocks.title: P4: choose a relevant card with your teacher
paragraphs: Card 1. A mistake to check: Every inland location is assumed to be high or mountainous. Better idea: Inland means away from the coast. A broad terrain description does not determine every local elevation. Reconnect: Separate coastal or inland labels from evidence about elevation or a particular route. Use the accepted records.

Card 2. A mistake to check: One observation or place description is treated as evidence about all communities. Better idea: Name the place and observation, limit the conclusion to that evidence and seek additional observations. Reconnect: Compare what the two club records actually describe. One record does not describe every place.

Card 3. A mistake to check: Coastal or inland is treated as enough evidence to select a safe site. Better idea: Compare the actual site, path and local observations. A region label alone does not establish safety. Reconnect: Match each room or route claim to its actual observation. A place name does not establish safety.

Card 4. A mistake to check: General coast-to-inland landform descriptions are treated as exact county boundaries. Better idea: Use an administrative map for county boundaries. A physical sketch does not establish those lines. Reconnect: Use separate labels for a physical region and an administrative county. They answer different kinds of questions.

Card 5. A mistake to check: Evidence about a dry room or a clear path is treated as proving the other requirement too. Better idea: Check each requirement separately. Room and route observations answer different questions. Reconnect: Make separate columns for room conditions and route access. Check each need with relevant evidence.

blocks.title: P5: choose a relevant card with your teacher
paragraphs: Card 1. A mistake to check: The variable's name is changed whenever its number changes. Better idea: Keep the name score fixed and replace the number stored beneath it. Reconnect: Keep the score name card fixed and replace only the number card when its value changes.

Card 2. A mistake to check: Set score to a number is treated as adding that number. Better idea: Set replaces the current value. Add uses the current value to calculate the next one. Reconnect: Compare set to 2 with add 2 from the same starting score of 4. Set replaces; add uses the previous value.

Card 3. A mistake to check: Initialization is repeated before every event, discarding the accumulated score. Better idea: Initialize at new-game start and retain the updated value between events. Reconnect: Initialize at the start of a new game. Keep the updated value between hits unless a reset event occurs.

Card 4. A mistake to check: A set instruction is ignored and the previous value is retained. Better idea: Follow every instruction in order. Set replaces the old value even if no points were earned. Reconnect: Follow every instruction in order, including set. Replace the number even when no points were earned.

Card 5. A mistake to check: A new game starts without initialization and inherits an earlier game's score. Better idea: Give each new game its stated starting value before processing events. Reconnect: Show the end of one game and the starting value of a new game on separate cards. Initialize the new game.

blocks.title: P6: choose a relevant card with your teacher
paragraphs: Card 1. A mistake to check: The switch creates the energy that lights the lamp. Better idea: The battery supplies energy. Closing the switch completes a conducting path; the switch does not create energy. Reconnect: Sketch the battery, lamp and conducting return path. Open and close the switch on the sketch.

Card 2. A mistake to check: One successful test proves the switch always works. Better idea: Record every trial, including failures. Five trials support a limited comparison, not a guarantee. Reconnect: Read every actual or explicitly supplied trial from the accepted Engineering activity. Include failures and identify the source.

Card 3. A mistake to check: Changing several components establishes which single change caused an outcome. Better idea: Change one contact feature while keeping battery, bulb, wires and procedure fixed. Reconnect: Name one contact feature to change. Keep battery, lamp, wires and procedure fixed.

Card 4. A mistake to check: The taller closed-switch bar proves the best design without checking open-switch control. Better idea: Use both closed-light and open-dark observations, and acknowledge the limits of the tests. Reconnect: Read both closed-light bars, then inspect both open-dark counts. Both criteria matter.

answerGuidance.math: 312 times 3 is 936: 900 + 30 + 6. Fresh retry 214 times 4 is 856: 800 + 40 + 16. Require value-preserving regrouping and an explanation.
answerGuidance.science: Food route and supporting-organ jobs stay distinct. Small intestine is the main absorption site. In the hypothetical paper model, 16 starting tokens = 6 transferred + 10 remaining. Tokens are not actual measurements of a person.
answerGuidance.english: Use the accepted text and its actual details; accept justified predictions or revisions, not invented endings. A summary identifies the main problem, response and result.
answerGuidance.socialStudies: Match room and route claims to separate evidence in the accepted records. Give a conditional recommendation. Do not infer elevation, all-site safety or county identity from a physical-region label.
answerGuidance.computing: Initial 3, hit 5, reset 1, hit 3. Fresh trace 1, add 3 gives 4, set to 2 gives 2, add 3 gives 5. State the starting value at a new game and retain the name while values change.
answerGuidance.engineering: Use the actual available trial/source record; never supply invented data. Explain complete/open paths, both criteria, one changed feature, controls and the limits of five trials. Without observations use a sketch/test-plan, not a fictional completed comparison.
answerGuidance.teaching: Select a card after the independent first attempt, model the idea, then collect a fresh independent explanation. These are feedback opportunities, not automatic diagnosis or persistent mastery evidence.

teacherGuide.selection: Six retrieval prompts cover the six periods. Use the actual response to select relevant cards with the learner. Cards are passive reference material, not 23 mandatory lessons. The teacher chooses a path; no automatic adaptive router is claimed.
teacherGuide.misconceptionScope: Each of the 23 accepted source misconceptions has a specifically attributed activity, guidance and retry card. The candidate declares two cross-cutting support misconceptions; source IDs on cards remain source references, not machine diagnoses or mastery updates.
teacherGuide.independentBoundary: Do not open guidance before the first attempt. Offer the matching fresh question without worked guidance; oral explanations or pupil-directed scribing are valid. A lesson not attempted is not a deficit.
teacherGuide.access: Read the selected card aloud; use paper, counters, labels and oral/scribed responses. No dragging, color, typing speed or network dependency. Keep examples separate from independent evidence.
teacherGuide.timing: 20 minutes is proposed, not measured. Use brief oral retrieval and one relevant card/retry; do not require every card or extension. Rehearsal remains a gate.
teacherGuide.extension: Offer the counterexample task when the teacher judges readiness from the work. Learners needing more practice explain their next relevant step instead; no self-declared mastery trigger.
teacherGuide.engineering: Preserve group-kit safety and rotation from P6. No kit or approved dataset is supplied here. Distinguish performed tests, group observation, analysed provided observations and sketch-only work.
teacherGuide.assessment: Formative only. No official grades, record writes, persistence or automatic mastery/diagnostic claims.

learnerFacingCards.text: Card 1. A mistake to check: The digits of a factor are multiplied as single units and their products are added. Better idea: Name the full place values before multiplying: 2 hundreds is 200, not 2. Reconnect: Represent 312 as 300, 10 and 2. Multiply each full value by 3 before combining.

Card 2. A mistake to check: Tens or hundreds formed by a partial product are discarded when writing the final digits. Better idea: Keep the value of every partial product and regroup it into the correct place rather than deleting it. Reconnect: Trade ten ones for one ten without throwing away value. Show how 4 times 4 ones becomes one ten and six ones.

Card 1. A mistake to check: The swallowed food route is drawn through the liver or pancreas instead of distinguishing the juices they supply. Better idea: Keep the continuous food route separate from the liver and pancreas, which supply digestive juices. Reconnect: Use one arrow for swallowed food and different arrows for digestive juices. Place liver and pancreas beside the food route.

Card 2. A mistake to check: The stomach is treated as the place where all nutrients enter the body. Better idea: Most digested nutrients are absorbed through the small-intestine wall. Reconnect: Compare the stomach with the small intestine. Locate where most digested nutrients enter the body.

accessibility.textAlternative: P2: choose a relevant card with your teacher. Card 1. A mistake to check: The swallowed food route is drawn through the liver or pancreas instead of distinguishing the juices they supply. Better idea: Keep the continuous food route separate from the liver and pancreas, which supply digestive juices. Reconnect: Use one arrow for swallowed food and different arrows for digestive juices. Place liver and pancreas beside the food route. Card 2. A mistake to check: The stomach is treated as the place where all nutrients enter the body. Better idea: Most digested nutrients are absorbed through the small-intestine wall. Reconnect: Compare the stomach with the small intestine. Locate where most digested nutrients enter the body. Card 3. A mistake to check: Nutrients that cross the wall are treated as disappearing from the model total. Better idea: Keep transferred tokens visible in the body region. Count both regions to conserve the total. Reconnect: Move paper nutrient tokens into a body region while keeping every token visible. Transferred tokens still exist. Card 4. A mistake to check: The starting count is reported as still inside after tokens have crossed the wall. Better idea: The starting count describes both regions together. Subtract transferred tokens to find what remains inside. Reconnect: Label the starting total before moving tokens. Label the tokens still in the first region separately. Card 5. A mistake to check: The number transferred during a round is confused with the number remaining inside. Better idea: Transferred and remaining name different groups. Track the inside count after every transfer. Reconnect: Keep transferred and remaining tokens in two labelled groups. Point to the group named by each question.

accessibility.textAlternative: P4: choose a relevant card with your teacher. Card 1. A mistake to check: Every inland location is assumed to be high or mountainous. Better idea: Inland means away from the coast. A broad terrain description does not determine every local elevation. Reconnect: Separate coastal or inland labels from evidence about elevation or a particular route. Use the accepted records. Card 2. A mistake to check: One observation or place description is treated as evidence about all communities. Better idea: Name the place and observation, limit the conclusion to that evidence and seek additional observations. Reconnect: Compare what the two club records actually describe. One record does not describe every place. Card 3. A mistake to check: Coastal or inland is treated as enough evidence to select a safe site. Better idea: Compare the actual site, path and local observations. A region label alone does not establish safety. Reconnect: Match each room or route claim to its actual observation. A place name does not establish safety. Card 4. A mistake to check: General coast-to-inland landform descriptions are treated as exact county boundaries. Better idea: Use an administrative map for county boundaries. A physical sketch does not establish those lines. Reconnect: Use separate labels for a physical region and an administrative county. They answer different kinds of questions. Card 5. A mistake to check: Evidence about a dry room or a clear path is treated as proving the other requirement too. Better idea: Check each requirement separately. Room and route observations answer different questions. Reconnect: Make separate columns for room conditions and route access. Check each need with relevant evidence.

accessibility.textAlternative: P5: choose a relevant card with your teacher. Card 1. A mistake to check: The variable's name is changed whenever its number changes. Better idea: Keep the name score fixed and replace the number stored beneath it. Reconnect: Keep the score name card fixed and replace only the number card when its value changes. Card 2. A mistake to check: Set score to a number is treated as adding that number. Better idea: Set replaces the current value. Add uses the current value to calculate the next one. Reconnect: Compare set to 2 with add 2 from the same starting score of 4. Set replaces; add uses the previous value. Card 3. A mistake to check: Initialization is repeated before every event, discarding the accumulated score. Better idea: Initialize at new-game start and retain the updated value between events. Reconnect: Initialize at the start of a new game. Keep the updated value between hits unless a reset event occurs. Card 4. A mistake to check: A set instruction is ignored and the previous value is retained. Better idea: Follow every instruction in order. Set replaces the old value even if no points were earned. Reconnect: Follow every instruction in order, including set. Replace the number even when no points were earned. Card 5. A mistake to check: A new game starts without initialization and inherits an earlier game's score. Better idea: Give each new game its stated starting value before processing events. Reconnect: Show the end of one game and the starting value of a new game on separate cards. Initialize the new game.

accessibility.textAlternative: P6: choose a relevant card with your teacher. Card 1. A mistake to check: The switch creates the energy that lights the lamp. Better idea: The battery supplies energy. Closing the switch completes a conducting path; the switch does not create energy. Reconnect: Sketch the battery, lamp and conducting return path. Open and close the switch on the sketch. Card 2. A mistake to check: One successful test proves the switch always works. Better idea: Record every trial, including failures. Five trials support a limited comparison, not a guarantee. Reconnect: Read every actual or explicitly supplied trial from the accepted Engineering activity. Include failures and identify the source. Card 3. A mistake to check: Changing several components establishes which single change caused an outcome. Better idea: Change one contact feature while keeping battery, bulb, wires and procedure fixed. Reconnect: Name one contact feature to change. Keep battery, lamp, wires and procedure fixed. Card 4. A mistake to check: The taller closed-switch bar proves the best design without checking open-switch control. Better idea: Use both closed-light and open-dark observations, and acknowledge the limits of the tests. Reconnect: Read both closed-light bars, then inspect both open-dark counts. Both criteria matter.

Guided reteach cards: choose a card with your teacher. Cover these cards during independent work.

P1 / Card 1. A mistake to check: The digits of a factor are multiplied as single units and their products are added. Better idea: Name the full place values before multiplying: 2 hundreds is 200, not 2. Reconnect: Represent 312 as 300, 10 and 2. Multiply each full value by 3 before combining.

P1 / Card 2. A mistake to check: Tens or hundreds formed by a partial product are discarded when writing the final digits. Better idea: Keep the value of every partial product and regroup it into the correct place rather than deleting it. Reconnect: Trade ten ones for one ten without throwing away value. Show how 4 times 4 ones becomes one ten and six ones.

P2 / Card 1. A mistake to check: The swallowed food route is drawn through the liver or pancreas instead of distinguishing the juices they supply. Better idea: Keep the continuous food route separate from the liver and pancreas, which supply digestive juices. Reconnect: Use one arrow for swallowed food and different arrows for digestive juices. Place liver and pancreas beside the food route.

P2 / Card 2. A mistake to check: The stomach is treated as the place where all nutrients enter the body. Better idea: Most digested nutrients are absorbed through the small-intestine wall. Reconnect: Compare the stomach with the small intestine. Locate where most digested nutrients enter the body.

P2 / Card 3. A mistake to check: Nutrients that cross the wall are treated as disappearing from the model total. Better idea: Keep transferred tokens visible in the body region. Count both regions to conserve the total. Reconnect: Move paper nutrient tokens into a body region while keeping every token visible. Transferred tokens still exist.

P2 / Card 4. A mistake to check: The starting count is reported as still inside after tokens have crossed the wall. Better idea: The starting count describes both regions together. Subtract transferred tokens to find what remains inside. Reconnect: Label the starting total before moving tokens. Label the tokens still in the first region separately.

P2 / Card 5. A mistake to check: The number transferred during a round is confused with the number remaining inside. Better idea: Transferred and remaining name different groups. Track the inside count after every transfer. Reconnect: Keep transferred and remaining tokens in two labelled groups. Point to the group named by each question.

P3 / Card 1. A mistake to check: A plausible prediction is reported as something the story has already established. Better idea: Name the detail that makes the idea plausible, use might or may, and change the prediction if later evidence conflicts. Reconnect: Mark an early clue, your prediction and a later detail in the accepted reading text. Treat the prediction as a possibility.

P3 / Card 2. A mistake to check: A summary lists incidental details or invents an outcome instead of connecting the central problem, response and result. Better idea: Keep the problem, the action taken and the result supported by the story; remove details that do not explain that connection. Reconnect: Choose details that explain the main problem, response and result. Put minor details aside.

P4 / Card 1. A mistake to check: Every inland location is assumed to be high or mountainous. Better idea: Inland means away from the coast. A broad terrain description does not determine every local elevation. Reconnect: Separate coastal or inland labels from evidence about elevation or a particular route. Use the accepted records.

P4 / Card 2. A mistake to check: One observation or place description is treated as evidence about all communities. Better idea: Name the place and observation, limit the conclusion to that evidence and seek additional observations. Reconnect: Compare what the two club records actually describe. One record does not describe every place.

P4 / Card 3. A mistake to check: Coastal or inland is treated as enough evidence to select a safe site. Better idea: Compare the actual site, path and local observations. A region label alone does not establish safety. Reconnect: Match each room or route claim to its actual observation. A place name does not establish safety.

P4 / Card 4. A mistake to check: General coast-to-inland landform descriptions are treated as exact county boundaries. Better idea: Use an administrative map for county boundaries. A physical sketch does not establish those lines. Reconnect: Use separate labels for a physical region and an administrative county. They answer different kinds of questions.

P4 / Card 5. A mistake to check: Evidence about a dry room or a clear path is treated as proving the other requirement too. Better idea: Check each requirement separately. Room and route observations answer different questions. Reconnect: Make separate columns for room conditions and route access. Check each need with relevant evidence.

P5 / Card 1. A mistake to check: The variable's name is changed whenever its number changes. Better idea: Keep the name score fixed and replace the number stored beneath it. Reconnect: Keep the score name card fixed and replace only the number card when its value changes.

P5 / Card 2. A mistake to check: Set score to a number is treated as adding that number. Better idea: Set replaces the current value. Add uses the current value to calculate the next one. Reconnect: Compare set to 2 with add 2 from the same starting score of 4. Set replaces; add uses the previous value.

P5 / Card 3. A mistake to check: Initialization is repeated before every event, discarding the accumulated score. Better idea: Initialize at new-game start and retain the updated value between events. Reconnect: Initialize at the start of a new game. Keep the updated value between hits unless a reset event occurs.

P5 / Card 4. A mistake to check: A set instruction is ignored and the previous value is retained. Better idea: Follow every instruction in order. Set replaces the old value even if no points were earned. Reconnect: Follow every instruction in order, including set. Replace the number even when no points were earned.

P5 / Card 5. A mistake to check: A new game starts without initialization and inherits an earlier game's score. Better idea: Give each new game its stated starting value before processing events. Reconnect: Show the end of one game and the starting value of a new game on separate cards. Initialize the new game.

P6 / Card 1. A mistake to check: The switch creates the energy that lights the lamp. Better idea: The battery supplies energy. Closing the switch completes a conducting path; the switch does not create energy. Reconnect: Sketch the battery, lamp and conducting return path. Open and close the switch on the sketch.

P6 / Card 2. A mistake to check: One successful test proves the switch always works. Better idea: Record every trial, including failures. Five trials support a limited comparison, not a guarantee. Reconnect: Read every actual or explicitly supplied trial from the accepted Engineering activity. Include failures and identify the source.

P6 / Card 3. A mistake to check: Changing several components establishes which single change caused an outcome. Better idea: Change one contact feature while keeping battery, bulb, wires and procedure fixed. Reconnect: Name one contact feature to change. Keep battery, lamp, wires and procedure fixed.

P6 / Card 4. A mistake to check: The taller closed-switch bar proves the best design without checking open-switch control. Better idea: Use both closed-light and open-dark observations, and acknowledge the limits of the tests. Reconnect: Read both closed-light bars, then inspect both open-dark counts. Both criteria matter.
